    People also ask
    Is Hanwha owned by Samsung?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    No, Hanwha is not owned by Samsung
    . In 2014-2015, Hanwha Group acquired Samsung Techwin (now Hanwha Vision) and Samsung Thales (now Hanwha Systems) from Samsung, making them independent subsidiaries of the Hanwha Group. Hanwha is a separate South Korean conglomerate, not a subsidiary of Samsung. 
    Key details regarding the acquisition include: 
    • Acquisition (2014-2015): Hanwha acquired 32.4% of Samsung Techwin and 57.6% of Samsung General Chemicals (now Hanwha Solutions).
    • Rebranding: Samsung Techwin was rebranded to Hanwha Techwin in 2016.
    • Independence: Hanwha and Samsung operate as entirely distinct corporate entities.
    • Defense & Tech:
      These divisions now form the core of Hanwha's aerospace and defense sectors, including Hanwha Aerospace.
       
    While formerly under the Samsung umbrella, these entities now belong to the Hanwha Group.

      AI Overview
      Hanwha Group's "net worth" varies by metric, but recent figures show its total assets around $107.4 billion to $113.2 billion (2023/2025 estimates) and a market cap for the core Hanwha Corporation around KRW 8.4 trillion (approx. $6-7 billion USD), with key subsidiaries like Hanwha Life holding over $82 billion in assets, reflecting a diversified conglomerate with substantial holdings across various industries, not a single net worth figure. 
      Key Figures & Metrics:
      • Total Assets (Group Level): Around $107.4B (2023) or $113.2B (2025 estimate). 
      • Hanwha Corporation (Market Cap): Approximately KRW 8.4 trillion (around $6-7 billion USD) as of early 2026. 
      • Hanwha Life (Assets): Exceeded 100 trillion KRW (over $82 billion USD) by late 2023. 
      • Hanwha Solutions (Market Cap): Around $5.92 billion USD as of March 2026. 
      Understanding Hanwha's Valuation:
      Hanwha is a large chaebol (South Korean conglomerate), so its "net worth" isn't a single number but a combination of its many listed and unlisted subsidiaries. Metrics like Total Assets (reflecting the overall size of the group's holdings) and Market Capitalization (the value of publicly traded shares for specific entities) are used. 
      In essence, Hanwha is a massive business group, with its core entity valued in the billions, while its total assets across all operations are in the hundreds of billions, with figures fluctuating based on the reporting period and specific companies included, notes Forbes and Stock Analysis.

        AI Overview
        Hanwha Group is led by Chairman Kim Seung-youn, who oversees the conglomerate, while his sons, including Kim Dong-kwan, hold key CEO positions in major subsidiaries like Hanwha Solutions and Hanwha Aerospace, managing daily operations and new growth engines as part of the family's succession plan.
         
        Key Leadership:
        • Kim Seung-youn (Chairman): The overall leader and strategist for the group, he receives significant compensation reflecting his role in future growth and M&A. 
        • Kim Dong-kwan (CEO & Director): A key figure in the succession, he's a CEO in several core businesses, including Hanwha Solutions. 
        • Seung Mo Kim (CEO & Chairman of Hanwha Corp): Leads the main holding company, Hanwha Corporation. 
        • Ki Won Yang (CEO & Director): Also a CEO and Director at Hanwha Corporation. 
        Leadership Structure:
        Hanwha operates with a structure where Chairman Kim Seung-youn sets the vision, while his sons and other appointed CEOs manage different sectors, driving innovation and market leadership.

          Main Businesses. What are the main businesses of Hanwha Group?
          About this result

          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          Hanwha Group's main businesses center around Energy & Ocean Solutions (solar, wind, hydrogen, marine), Aerospace & Mechatronics (defense, aviation, robotics), Finance (insurance, asset management, digital finance), and Retail & Services (department stores, resorts, lifestyle). They leverage synergy across these diversified sectors, including chemicals, advanced materials, and construction, to provide innovative and sustainable solutions globally, making them a major South Korean conglomerate. 
          Key Business Areas:
          • Energy & Ocean Solutions:
            • Solar: Qcells (solar cells/modules, power plants). 
            • Wind & Hydrogen: Developing renewable energy projects. 
            • Marine: Hanwha Ocean (shipbuilding, maritime defense).
          • Aerospace & Mechatronics:
            • Aerospace: Aircraft engines, launch vehicles, satellites (Hanwha Aerospace).
            • Defense: Land, sea, and space defense systems. 
            • Robotics: Advanced robotics (Hanwha Robotics).
          • Finance:
            • Insurance: Hanwha Life (insurance, digital finance).
            • Securities & Asset Management: .
          • Retail & Services:
            • Lifestyle: Department stores (Galleria), resorts, hotels, golf courses. 
          • Chemicals & Advanced Materials:
            • Petrochemicals, synthetic resins, lightweight composites (Hanwha Solutions, Hanwha Advanced Materials). 
          • Construction:
            • Engineering, complex development, and general construction. 
          How they operate:
          Hanwha uses its broad portfolio to create integrated solutions, for example, combining aerospace technology with defense, or using chemical expertise in new materials. They focus on sustainability, addressing climate change through green energy and decarbonization efforts.

            History. What is the history of Hanwha Group?
            About this result
            Feedback
            An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
            AI Overview
            Hanwha Group started as Korea Explosives Co. in 1952, founded by Kim Chong-hee to supply explosives for South Korea's post-war reconstruction, and grew from basic industrial materials into a major global conglomerate with diverse interests in aerospace, energy (especially solar), chemicals, finance, and retail. Its history involves strategic diversification, significant global acquisitions (like Q.CELLS), and key role in Korea's industrial development, becoming the nation's seventh-largest business group by 2024.
             
            Early Years & Foundation (1950s-1970s)
            • 1952: Founded as Korea Explosives Co., producing industrial explosives for rebuilding the country. 
            • 1959: Became the second Asian company to produce nitroglycerin. 
            • Expansion: Moved into chemicals, including petrochemicals and PVC, and broadened its focus beyond explosives. 
            Diversification & Growth (1980s-2000s)
            • Financial Services: Entered finance with Hanwha Life Insurance (originally Korea Life Insurance). 
            • Aerospace: The entity that became Hanwha Aerospace started as Samsung Precision in 1977, focusing on defense and precision engineering. 
            • Global Expansion: Began international growth in the early 2000s, acquiring U.S. and European automotive component makers. 
            Global Leadership & Modern Era (2010s-Present)
            • Solar Power: Became a global leader in solar energy by acquiring Solarfun (later Hanwha Solutions) and Q.CELLS, establishing major production. 
            • Aerospace & Defense: Expanded aerospace capabilities, including aircraft engines and satellite communications (e.g., OneWeb stake). 
            • Energy Transition: Increased focus on sustainable energy, including wind, hydrogen, and eco-friendly materials. 
            • Key Acquisitions: Acquired Samsung Techwin (now Hanwha Vision) and other defense assets, further solidifying its technology and defense presence. 
            Core Business Areas Today
            • Energy & Materials: Solar, petrochemicals, advanced materials. 
            • Aerospace & Defense: Space, aircraft engines, defense systems.
            • Finance: Insurance, securities, asset management. 
            • Retail & Services: Hotels, resorts, department stores, large complexes.

              Hanwha Group's key milestones center on diversification from explosives into solar energy (Q CELLS acquisition), advanced defense (aerospace, radar), petrochemicals, and future tech like AI/UAM, marked by major acquisitions (Samsung affiliates, DSME as Hanwha Ocean), global expansion (US solar hub), and significant defense contracts (Poland, Australia), showcasing a pivot towards green energy and cutting-edge technology.
               
              Key Milestones by Sector:
              • Energy & Sustainability:
                • 2010/2012: Acquired Solarfun Power & Q.CELLS, becoming a global solar leader. 
                • 2020s: Focused on green hydrogen, advanced solar tech (perovskite), and renewable energy goals (100% renewable by 2050). 
                • 2023/2024: Launched major solar module production in the US and expanded into global shipbuilding (Hanwha Ocean). 
              • Defense & Aerospace:
                • 2014: Acquired Samsung Techwin, Samsung Thales, boosting defense. 
                • 2020s: Developed AESA radar, entered Urban Air Mobility (UAM), and secured large defense exports (UAE, Poland). 
                • 2023: Won major Redback IFV contract in Australia. 
              • Petrochemicals & Materials:
                • 1960s: Entered petrochemicals with PVC and LDPE production. 
                • 2014: Acquired Samsung General Chemicals, expanding petrochemical footprint. 
              • Financial Services & Other:
                • 2002: Acquired Korea Life Insurance, shifting focus to finance. 
              • Technology & Future Growth:
                • 2020s: Invested in satellite communications (OneWeb, Phasor), AI/Cloud (Hanwha Vision), and space tech (Nuri rocket support). 
              Overall Evolution:
              From its roots in explosives (1950s) to a global conglomerate, Hanwha's journey highlights strategic acquisitions and diversification, especially in green energy and defense, positioning itself for future technologies.
